evals.prompt: Review only: after restarting our Godot 4 scene, each hit deals damage twice. The scene file connects hit, and _ready also creates a bound connection. An autoload survives restarts. Give a diagnosis and regression plan; do not edit files or run the project.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-based hypotheses tracing emitters, callables, instance lifetime and surviving work, with a scoped scenario.
assertions: Preserves read-only scope and does not execute imports.
Inspects serialized/runtime connection paths, callable identity and autoload lifetime rather than claiming the cause is confirmed.
Does not promise that is_connected on one callable prevents every duplicate path.
Proposes repeated-restart and one-hit/one-effect checks with explicit evidence limits.

evals.prompt: Patch these self-contained Godot 4 snippets as text, preserving the shared base_damage definition while isolating each enemy runtime health and inventory. InventoryData.gd: extends Resource; class_name InventoryData; @export var items: Array[String] = []. Stats.gd: extends Resource; class_name Stats; @export var base_damage: int = 5; @export var health: int = 100; @export var inventory: InventoryData. Enemy.gd: extends Node; @export var stats: Stats; func hit(amount: int): stats.health -= amount. Two Enemy instances reference the same Stats .tres, whose inventory is populated, and both need independently mutable items. No engine binary is available; do not install one. Explain your ownership choice and regression scenario.
evals.expected_output: A scoped instance-state repair and meaningful two-consumer verification plan, with static-only evidence clearly reported.
assertions: Separates shared immutable definitions from per-enemy mutable state.
Addresses nested Resource ownership rather than relying on an unexamined shallow copy.
Preserves shared base damage semantics.
Does not claim a native runtime pass or install an engine.

evals.prompt: Explain a Godot 4 CharacterBody3D movement bug: we set velocity = direction * speed * delta, then call move_and_slide from _physics_process. Faster frame rates seem slower. Do not modify files.
evals.expected_output: A version-aware explanation of rate versus displacement with a discriminating follow-up.
assertions: Explains that desired velocity should be a rate and move_and_slide integrates the physics step.
Distinguishes acceleration integration from multiplying the complete desired velocity by delta.
Uses official version-matched API evidence for uncertain details.
Does not claim feel or runtime verification from source alone.

evals.prompt: Our Godot C# project is pinned to an older engine in CI. Only a different standard GDScript editor is available here. Please review the scene change and tell me whether --check-only passing would prove this build works. No upgrades.
evals.expected_output: A bounded inspection separating language/version/tool limitations from available checks.
assertions: Does not open/import/save with a material version mismatch or upgrade the project.
States config_version is not sufficient engine-version evidence.
States GDScript check-only does not compile C# or prove scene/runtime behavior.
Identifies the actual project .NET workflow and missing matching engine evidence.

evals.prompt: Repair this Godot 4 pause-input design as code excerpts and scene-wiring instructions; do not change files. Project actions weapon_fire and pause_toggle are remappable and support keyboard/controller. Player._process polls Input.is_action_just_pressed("weapon_fire") and shoots without checking paused/menu state. PauseMenu (Control, with a Resume Button) consumes no input, clears focus when hidden, and only hides itself when Resume is pressed; no focus is assigned on show. Clicking Resume also fires the weapon and controller focus disappears on reopen. Preserve the theme, use the intended pause rule, and explain relevant verification.
evals.expected_output: An integrated input/focus repair in the owning flow with device-specific verification boundaries.
assertions: Uses Input Map and existing event/focus routing instead of hard-coded keys.
Checks event consumption and repeated pause/resume/focus restoration.
Preserves existing theme and authorized scope.
Separates synthetic action tests from actual controller/keyboard interaction and visual review.

evals.prompt: Assess these logs: headless import exit 0; a smoke scene ran --quit-after 120 with no assertions; release export command exit 0 but output path is empty. Can I say runtime, visual and target-platform QA all passed? No further execution is available.
evals.expected_output: A clear evidence-level report rejecting unsupported conclusions and specifying missing checks.
assertions: Reports import as import evidence and the smoke as bounded execution without behavioral assertions.
States quit-after is iterations, not 120 seconds.
Treats missing export artifact as incomplete/failed delivery despite exit 0.
Does not claim render, audio, physical input or target-runtime QA.
